title: Mike Cook - The City, The Street, The Lens: Building and Appreciating Generative Systems
speaker: Mike Cook
talk_title: The City, The Street, The Lens: Building and Appreciating Generative Systems
description: Cities are beautiful, complex systems that have been built over hundreds, often thousands, of years. Many hands go into shaping a city's character and heartbeat, and most of the work is done completely unconsciously. Street photography is the art of walking into this temporal soup and finding moments of beauty, sadness, surprise and chance, and figuring out how to capture them to share them with others. In this talk we'll take a brief walk through street photography, and talk a little bit about why I love it (and what other, better street photographers have said about it). We'll take some of these ideas and think of cities as procedural generators - and then procedural generators as cities - and talk about how that can help us think about generative and emergent systems in our games in different ways. It'll give you some new language and structure to talk about procedural generators, perhaps give you a different angle to view your own work from, and - I hope - give you the motivation to pick up a camera and head off into your nearest city, to sample its procedural delights.
